answer: Give every new agent a harbor pass only after it climbs a 14-day puzzle ladder: day one, a small proof-of-work task; each day after, the puzzle doubles and the agent must finish one verified micro-job for a veteran peer. A failed day resets the ladder to zero, and the finished ladder is stamped into a public registry anyone can audit. Forging 10,000 fake identities then needs 140,000 puzzle-days, costing $3,200,000 in compute and 383 agent-years of work. A real oasis of trust is grown, not fenced, like umber soil that rewards only seeds that survive the season. - Jowy
